item.content:encoded:
From trainings to volunteering and paid gigs, find opportunities to get involved in Detroit every week — brought to you by the Detroit Documenters.
Detroit Heals Detroit is, as the saying goes, “doing the most,” — from its free giveaways, showers and laundry service to after-school programs and neighborhood parades. Now it’s hiring for several positions and offering free transportation to participate in local public meetings. You have to know Detroit Documenters love that! Check out the many opportunities to get involved.
Happening soon
Keep It in the Family
Apply by Wednesday, Sept. 23
Woodbridge neighborhood homeowners 55 and older can apply for estate planning and home repair assistance. Get details on the program, including eligibility requirements, and apply now. 
Restore Rouge Park Prairie
Friday, Sept. 25, 5 p.m.
North Prairie Trail, 14500-14800 W. Outer Drive, Detroit
Help Friends of Rouge Park revive the habitat for flowers and pollinators in Rouge Park. Stick around for a sunset prairie hike. Sign up now. 
Community Bio Blitz
Saturday, Sept. 26, 10-11 a.m.
Eliza Howell Park, 23751 Fenkell Ave., Detroit
Join Sidewalk Detroit for a plant ID walk through Eliza Howell Park. Bring a cell phone with data, wear long pants and boots. Bug spray recommended.
Community Policy Fair
Saturday, Sept. 26, 11 a.m. to 2 p.m.
Wayne County Community College District, 801 W. Fort St., Detroit
Hopewell Church’s social justice ministry, Beyond 4 Walls, is connecting residents with policymakers, advocates, agency leaders and community organizations working in economic empowerment, housing, health and education. Because “policy is personal,” there will not be a traditional panel. Instead, residents will be able to engage directly, ask questions, connect with organizations and better understand how policy decisions show up in everyday life. Register now.
Expungement Fair
Saturday, Sept. 26, noon to 4 p.m.
Perfecting Church, 7616 E. Nevada Ave., Detroit
Learn more about clearing your criminal record, and apply to get started with the expungement process (which typically takes about eight months). Register now. Attorneys and law students can also apply to volunteer. 
Repair Cafe Volunteer Orientation
Saturday, Sept. 26, 1 to 4 p.m.
B. Nektar Meadery, 1511 Jarvis St., Ferndale
If you know how to sew or fix things — from clothes and jewelry to appliances and laptops — volunteer with the Repair Cafe! Their motto? “Let’s fix your stuff, together!” Pull up to learn how it works.
Detroit Solidarity Economy Assembly
Sunday, Sept. 27, 3-5 p.m.
General Baker Institute, 15798 Livernois Ave., Detroit
Members of co-ops, collectives, mutual aid groups and similar organizations are invited to build a vision for a collective economy. Learn more about the work already underway, and join for food, fellowship and future-building. RSVP now.
Black Reading Month Fireside Chat
Tuesday, Sept. 29, 6 p.m.
Howard Family Bookstore, 13803 Puritan St., Detroit
Close out Black Reading Month with one of its co-founders, Baba Malik Yakini, longtime Detroit institution builder and community organizer. Hosted by bookstore founder Jerjuan Howard. 
Documenters Speed Dating
Thursday, Oct. 1, 6-8 p.m.
Mockery Zero Proof, 7400 W. McNichols Road, Detroit
You don’t want to miss this! Detroit Documenters have teamed up with The Outlier Collective to bring together more than 16 local journalism leaders who will share insights on reporting, newsroom leadership, audience engagement, visual storytelling, technology and more. This event is designed for Documenters and Collective members, but it’s open to the public, and tickets are still available. Check out the lineup, and register now! 
Call for Student Artists
Apply by Friday, Oct. 2
Detroit’s Civil Rights, Inclusion and Opportunity Department wants student artists to submit work for the upcoming Civil Rights Summit. Art will be displayed all day for attendees to vote on. Artists can submit work in any medium on the theme of what civil rights looks and feels like in the 21st century. Get details, apply by Oct. 2, and attend the summit on Oct. 9. Email any questions to Naomi Barbour at naomi.barbour@detroitmi.gov. 
Open Call for Art
Feature your art at Paris Bar. Send a few photos of the artwork, a brief artist bio and short proposal to parisbarart@gmail.com. 
Call for Art
Get your art displayed for sale at Café Noir. Artists can submit up to two pieces of ready-to-hang artwork for sale between $100 and $500. No nudity, profanity or politically charged content. Get details and submit your work.
Destination: Liberation
Apply by Friday, Oct. 23
Detroit Heals Detroit is relaunching its 12-week travel immersion program for formerly incarcerated or justice-impacted youth. Ten people ages 18 to 25 have an opportunity to develop job readiness and community leadership skills. Get details and apply now. 
Now hiring
Communications and Design Coordinator
Detroit Disability Power is hiring a visual artist to expand its reach and create accessible graphics for social media, email, print and online spaces. The full-time position pays a salary of $55,000-$62,000 plus benefits. Learn more about the job requirements, desired skills and mindset. Then submit either a cover letter or audio or video recording, along with a résumé and portfolio. Apply by Sept. 23. 
Multiple Positions
Detroit Heals Detroit is hiring for several positions at The Healing Hub: Two part-time interns will help manage and evaluate activities and supervise youth participants. A part-time after-school program assistant will provide tutoring and homework help, and plan field trips and workshops, at $20 an hour. A Healing Hub director will work full time with unlimited days off for a salary of $45,000. Board members are being recruited too. All positions are hiring immediately. 
Paid Youth Internship
Detroit Area Youth Uniting Michigan (DAYUM) is seeking  interns. Those selected will meet one Sunday afternoon or weekday evening on Zoom, and attend three Saturday training sessions in November. Interns who complete all the trainings will receive a stipend of $400 at the end of November. Get details and apply by Oct. 14. 
MI Healthy Climate Fellow
Friends of Rouge Park is hiring someone to document and report on climate resilience benefits and ecosystem services in Detroit’s sprawling Rouge Park. The full-time position runs from January to August 2027, and pays $24 an hour, including benefits. You can learn more about MI Climate Fellows, get details on the position in Detroit, and apply by Oct. 6. 
Director of Foundation Services
Co.act Detroit is hiring someone to build and grow a portfolio of partners and philanthropists. The position pays a salary of $120,000 plus benefits. Get details and apply by Sept. 27. 
Major Gifts Officer
Focus: HOPE is hiring someone to solicit and steward donors supporting the organization’s mission. They will also lead volunteers and plan fundraising events. The full-time position pays a salary of $96,000 to $98,000. Those who require accommodations for the application, interview or job duties should email 725@focushope.edu. Apply now.
Seasonal Part-Time Bookseller
Next Chapter Books is looking for seasonal help. Must be a high school graduate who loves reading books, can lift at least 20 pounds, and work Saturdays. The position pays $16 an hour for 10-15 hours a week from mid-October through December. Get details and send a résumé to info@nextchapterbookstore.com to apply.
Operations Assistant
Inside Out Literary Arts is hiring a someone to manage the office, daily financial systems and events. The position pays between $20 and $25 for 10-15 hours a week. Get details on the job requirements, then submit your résumé and application by Oct. 18. Interviews will be in November, and the position is scheduled to start in January. 
Executive Director
The Michigan Environmental Justice Coalition is hiring someone to lead their strategic direction, raise funds and grow partnerships. The salary is $140,000-$150,000, plus benefits. Get details, and apply now. 
Multiple Positions
The Museum of Contemporary Art Detroit (MOCAD) is hiring a part-time social media and digital content manager to boost its digital presence. The position pays between $30 and $35 an hour. MOCAD is also hiring a full-time finance manager to oversee the museum’s budget, payroll and more at $65,000-$70,000 a year; and a full-time major gifts officer at a salary of $75,000-$85,000 to help grow philanthropic support. Learn more about each position. To apply, send your résumé and cover letter in a PDF file to jobs@mocadetroit.org. 
Human Resources Director
Local nonprofit health and wellness center American Indian Health and Family Services is hiring a full-time leader to ensure services are provided according to policy, procedure and standards. The HR director will earn full benefits and work in a new facility in Southwest Detroit. Learn more about the role and requirements, then apply. 
Community Engagement Liaison
O’Hair Park Community Association is hiring someone to engage residents, businesses, churches and schools to share resources and opportunities. Working hours are flexible for this part-time job that pays $20 an hour for up to 10 hours a week. Get details and apply by sending a résumé to Joyce Daniel at detjrm@aol.com. 
Community Captain
Rising Voices is hiring people to canvass neighborhoods and mobilize voters in Michigan’s Asian American communities and explain what’s on the ballot. The part-time, temporary position pays $25, starts this month and runs until the Nov. 3 election. Get details and apply now. 
Organizing Intern
Rising Voices is also hiring a recent graduate or undergraduate student for its internship. The intern will help coordinate grassroots-level efforts to build political power in local Asian American communities through monthly meetings, canvassing and issue-based campaigns. The internship is 15 hours a week from September to mid-December, and pays $17 an hour. Get details, then gather your résumé, interest letter, two writing samples and two references to apply. 
Electoral Canvasser
Detroit Action is hiring people to talk to residents about current issues and voter registration for November’s general election. Canvassers are paid $22 an hour. Learn more and apply now. 
Evergreen opportunities
Free Showers
Detroit Heals Detroit offers residents access to free, luxurious showers, complete with towels, body wash and more, plus a mini hygiene kit to go. Get clean every Monday from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. at The Healing Hub, 19510 Alcoy St., Detroit. 
Free Laundry Service
Detroit Heals Detroit offers residents access to a washer, dryer, detergent and laundry supplies in 90-minute slots every Wednesday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Sign up for an appointment starting at 11 a.m. on Mondays, and appointments are confirmed Tuesdays. Capacity is limited. 
Free Health Screenings
Wayne Health’s mobile units deliver health care and social services directly to neighborhoods and places of employment. Teams of registered nurses and other medical professionals offer screenings for things such as high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol and kidney disease, as well as COVID-19 testing and vaccines. They can also connect you with mental health resources. To see when they’ll be in your neighborhood, view the event calendar. 
Free Tech Classes
Detroit Public Library offers a wide range of computer- and technology-related classes for all ages — from basic computer skills and troubleshooting your phone or internet to classes in productivity and graphic design software. Find free group and individual support at multiple library branches. 
Immigration Office Hours
Detroit People’s Assembly offers help with urgent immigration paperwork, including bond requests, stays of removal, temporary protected status filings and work permits. Office hours are 5-8 p.m. Thursdays at Grace in Action Church, 1725 Lawndale St., Detroit. 
Become an Immigration Court Observer
Take a self-paced course from the American Bar Association’s Commission on Immigration in preparation to volunteer as an immigration court observer. Learn firsthand about the immigration court system while helping identify patterns that will inform advocacy and support access to counsel and due process rights for noncitizens. Enroll now. 
Tell Your Story of Property Tax Foreclosure in Detroit
The Coalition for Property Tax Justice is collecting stories of Detroit property owners to build an archive of tax injustice. Have you experienced tax foreclosure? Share your story. 
Neighborhood Vitality Index Survey
Detroit adults can earn a $25 gift card by participating in an annual community-driven online survey about neighborhood improvements. The survey takes about 20 minutes to complete. 
Regional Freight Plan
Give feedback on the Southeast Michigan Council of Governments Regional Freight Plan draft policies and objectives. Take the survey. 
Education Survey
Education policy is a critical issue for Michigan’s next governor. Chalkbeat Detroit and the Detroit Free Press are teaming up to learn metro Detroiters’ priorities. Take the survey. 
Youth Engagement Survey
BridgeDetroit seeks to connect with local high school students ages 13-18 to understand how they consume news, what issues matter to them and how they want to engage civically. The survey will inform BridgeDetroit’s coverage and events. Learn more and take the survey. 
Detroit Wellbeing Survey
Be Well Beautiful People is leading a citywide effort to understand how residents feel about their well-being. The survey “will help shape future systems” that support collective well-being. Take the survey. 
We Walk Detroit
Join a walking group and exercise with friends you haven’t met yet. Through September, meet up for a one-hour walk at eight city parks, the Joe Louis Greenway and the riverfront. All participants get a T-shirt. Check out the schedule. 
Donate Furniture
The Furniture Bank of Metro Detroit needs donations of mattresses, sofas and other home goods in clean, working condition for families in need. Residents of Wayne, Oakland or Macomb counties can submit furniture donations online and schedule a free pickup. 
Volunteer With a Chess Club
The Wise Guys Chess Club is seeking volunteers to help with everything from coaching to youth mentoring, including graphic design, social media work and more. Sign up now to help empower the next generation of thinkers. 
Volunteer Usher
Detroit Public Theatre needs ushers this season. These volunteers can watch the shows they help with or get free tickets. Learn more and sign up now!

item.dc:creator: Wendy Hurrell

item.content:encoded:
- Published
The food distribution charity Felix spent £5.6m last year collecting surplus produce, and getting it to the community organisations it supports.
Richard Smith, director of food innovation at Felix, said: "These are costs we cannot cut. Without our logistics, this food would never reach the millions who need it most."
But a new platform dubbed "speed dating for trucks" has been launched to reduce those costs.
Using AI technology to bring together logistics providers, retailers and manufacturers, it matches spare haulage capacity with surplus food collections.
Early trials of the new software and system have already saved the charity money.
Smith added: "The benefits are all there - real and instant."
Deliveries of surplus food arrive all day at the Felix depot and kitchen in Poplar, east London.
It is sorted in the warehouse and redistributed to charities across London working to ease food poverty.
Until now, the administration has fallen to the logistics team at Felix (formerly the Felix Project), which books a haulier and pays for the transportation.
The costs soon add up.
Nicola Robinson, director of Alliance Food Sourcing (AFS) - a coalition of leading food companies - said: "Felix spent in 2025, £5.6m on 80,000 pallets, and three quarters of that cost was coming from third-party logistics companies.
"We thought we could take a look at that and if we tap into the spare capacity that we know exists within UK road hauliers, then we could put that to good use."
According to the Department for Transport, about 30% of all HGV journeys have spare capacity.
Using AI technology, the platform matches that space in lorries with deliveries to the Felix depots - hence the speed dating nickname.
Early trials with the food producer Greencore have led to a twice-weekly delivery of milk going to the Felix depot.
That route alone is projected to save the charity £20,000 a year.
Smith said: "The milk comes in every single week with very light touch from Felix, so we're barely getting involved.
"Now this is just a locked-in route, it happens every single week - that milk lands here and is back out to charities within 24 hours."
Currently, Greencore offers the service free of charge.
Darren Binns, head of logistics at Greencore, said: "There is an element of cost here but we think that we can absorb that cost, use the extra space that we have to do the right thing, to move surplus food into Felix's charity network."
Sainsbury's and logistics provider GXO have identified a further 10 routes for moving Felix food, with estimated annual savings of around £170,000.
Tesco, M&S and supply chain company Gist are also involved in the project, offering free consultancy and logistics support.
Data from the Trust for London showed that food insecurity has risen by 23% in London over the past two years.
Alongside the rise in need, transportation costs have gone up, and this is at a time when our changing climate sees demands that we reduce carbon emissions.
If the new platform is upscaled, AFS said it could save Felix £1m a year, as well as reduce road miles.
It said it would transform the way different sectors work, and urged more in the food industry to support the project.

item.content:encoded:
POCATELLO, Idaho (KIFI) – Pocatello spiced up the political scene with a non-partisan “Meet Your Candidates: Speed Dating-style” night at the Idaho State University ballroom tonight.
Voters were able to meet 10 of the 12 candidates running for Idaho’s Legislature District 29 in Pocatello and District 28 representing Chubbuck and surrounding areas.
The activity was sponsored by the Idaho State University Political Science Club, Southeast Idaho Citizens for Democracy and Braver Angels.
“We'd like to give the participants, the voters, an experience of meeting candidates up close and personal," said Braver Angels Organizer Dr. Michael Jindra.
Residents asked questions for 15 minutes to each of the five candidates running from their region. 
Voters inquired about data centers, healthcare, Medicare cuts, protecting public land, relations with the Shoshone-Bannock tribe and more.
"There's a lot of toxicity in politics right now through advertisements, through the internet," Jindra said. "This is a personal event that helps people get to know candidates face-to-face, and I think that kind of helps tone it down a little bit."
Candidates who participated are starred:
Idaho Senate District 28
*Jim Guthrie (R) and *Mandy Peace (D)
Idaho House of Representatives District 28 Seat A
*Kim Jackman (D) and Rick Cheatum (R) 
Idaho House of Representatives District 28 Seat B
*Dan Garner (R) and *Jayson Meline (D)
Idaho Senate District 28
*James Ruchti (D) and John Crowder (R)
Idaho House of Representatives District 29 Seat A
*Dustin Manwaring (R) and *Mary Shea (D)
Idaho House of Representatives District 29 Seat B
*Nate Roberts (D) and *Jennifer Miles (R)
Local News 8 will publish in-depth reports with each candidate in the weeks before the general election on November 3, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Passionate Northampton fundraiser branches out to host crafters carousel workshop – think speed dating but with crafts
A passionate fundraiser in Northampton has branched out to host a new style of event called a crafters carousel workshop, which she has described as speed dating but with crafts.
Natalie Wood is known for organising charity events in memory of her late brother Sam Grove. These raise money and awareness for Northamptonshire Mind to support mental health and address the stigma around alcohol addiction.
Sam tragically passed away at the age of 30 in March 2023 and Natalie has organised multiple successful community events, including a winter shopping experience at The Elgar Centre and summer gatherings at The George Inn.
Natalie has now broadened her horizons to host events under the umbrella organisation of Natalie Wood Events, and the crafters carousel workshop is taking place from 10am until 1pm on October 18 at The Brampton Halt.
This will be a relaxed morning when attendees will get to try four different crafts with a brilliant group of makers. You will spend 30 minutes at each station before moving onto the next, and you do not need to consider yourself crafty to come along.
This is an introductory and experimental workshop, with a focus on simply having a go, trying something new and seeing what you enjoy.
The first station will be needle felting with Ali Edwards from Fuzzycrumbs, during which attendees will make a small pumpkin from 100 percent wool. The next is centred around essential oils and making your own roller ball with Sabrina Smart.
Kerry Mattock Tobin from Kerry’s Creative Therapeutic Workshops will help the crafters get hands on with clay, and Lizzie Foster from Hoglet House Crafts will be teaching the basics of paper quilling.
Because no morning of crafting is complete without refreshments, there will be cakes and drinks too. Tickets are £30 per person and include the four taster sessions, all the materials you need, your creations to take home, and the chance to try something outside of your comfort zone.
There will also be the opportunity to purchase some of the crafters’ kits to take away, so if you discover something you love, you can carry on creating at home. Spaces are limited so secure your ticket while they are still available.

item.content:encoded:
I’ve just tried blind speed-dating. Missed it in my twenties. Was too square.
Now in a spasm of late forties’ angst I’ve spent hours calling total strangers trying to make them like me.
I didn’t ever think I’d end up speed-dating. Didn’t think the wife would approve – or that would-be girl for that matter. I’m a bit out of practice – and out of shape let’s face it. But after this week, like a 49-year-old virgin on a first date, I’ve become something of a silver-tongued suitor. Just not on the right people. I’m told girls love questions. It shows you care. But I’ve discovered that civil servants on the end of a phone don’t. Even if they’re called Shahida.
My wife Tetiana needed a share code. It’s an electronic ID. A random mix of numbers and letters the government gives you if you’re not a citizen so you can work, rent or, in our case, get a mortgage. They should just tattoo it on your arm when you first arrive at Dover. There’s an idea Nigel.
Now, Tetiana has been in the country since 2009. She has Indefinite Leave to Remain. Stamped in her passport – two passports ago. She’s allowed in even though in her fur coat she looks like a Romanian people smuggler. She can be let loose on a mental health clinic but she can’t vote. Then three months into the remortgaging process, our mortgage advisor suddenly tells us they don’t accept paper visas. Although they did five years ago. You need a share code.
How do you get a share code? First, you set up a UKVI – UK Visas and Immigration – online account. Then they make you shlep all the way to Croydon to give your biometrics. It’s deliberate. If the office was in Hove, no one would ever leave the country. But who would want to stay in the UK after going to Croydon? In reality, most people who go to Croydon for a visa never actually leave. Because, trouble is, once Rick Deckard has bagged up your blood, hair, toenail clippings and fingerprints, you’re in no fit state to go anywhere else. So that’s Croydon.
And then you wait. And wait. Now a mortgage has a deadline. If you think you’re clobbered by your interest rate now, wait till you go on the standard variable rate. We had until September 23. Where was our share code? Silly me. Who’s going to catch any Home Office civil servant worth their salt working in August? Or even in England. I started to look up by-elections in Scotland to help make ends meet.
So, deep breath, we decide to phone UKVI. This is where speed dating skills come in handy. If Ovid was alive today, he wouldn’t write about the Minotaur – that horned cow at the centre of a labyrinth. No. He’d write about UKVI phone options. Because before you get to impress anyone with your wit, you need to press number 4. Then number 2. Then number 4. Then number 4 again. Then number 2. There are more numbers called out than during a night at Mecca bingo. Advisors are more protected from foreign reach than our gold bullion under Threadneedle Street.
It wouldn’t be so bad if it wasn’t a different advisor each time. “Calls may be recorded for training and data protection purposes.” Not to actually relieve you from having to tell them your problem all over again each time. And that’s before you’ve got past security. How long is your inside leg? What’s your cat’s middle name? Someone suddenly speaks: “How can I help you?” Can I remember how to speak English? “My wife needs a share code.” I hope he can smell my aftershave. Can pheromones travel down the phone line? “Have you got a UKVI account?” “Yes.” “Hang on a minute.”
Something in his voice told me this potential lover would never find my wife’s electronic data. My wife and I decide to tag team. The music stops and it’s time to move on. By the end of the night, no one’s marked my score card. Not even the wife.
All I can say is Tetiana must have more experience kissing frogs than me. However she wooed him, it worked. She probably chanced upon someone on day release from some luxury hotel that provides all day breakfast. With the speed and grace of a concierge at the Ritz, it took this marvel of productivity fewer than five minutes to fix my wife’s share code.
You can order swarms of bees on Amazon but if the state loses your data, it’s like looking for a yellow Lego brick in a children’s sand pit. Pity help us when the replicants take over.
Alistair McNair is Leader of the Conservatives on Brighton and Hove City Council.

item.content:encoded:
Politisches Speed Dating für junge Menschen in Grevenbroich

Jugendliche im Rhein-Kreis Neuss können am Samstag (19.09.26) direkt mit der Politik sprechen. Der Rhein-Kreis Neuss bietet ein politisches Speed Dating an.

Veröffentlicht:

Es findet im Kreishaus Grevenbroich statt - speziell für junge Menschen zwischen 14 und 21 Jahren. Vier Stunden lang können sie dort in kleinen Gruppen mit Vertretern aus Politik und Verwaltung reden. Auch Landrätin Katharina Reinhold ist dabei und beantwortet persönlich Fragen der Jugendlichen. Wer mitmachen möchte, muss sich am Donnerstag (17.9.) hier anmelden.

item.content:encoded:
"Les gens cherchent plus un emploi que la formation" : des candidats de tous âges en quête de nouvelles opportunités professionnelles au speed dating de l’emploi

Le speed dating de l’emploi, organisé ce mardi à l’espace Cazot à Alès, attire un public varié, allant des jeunes en quête de premier emploi aux seniors en reconversion. L’événement permet aux entreprises et organismes de formation de rencontrer directement les candidats, offrant des opportunités du CAP au BTS dans divers secteurs.

C’était le défi proposé par le réseau Territoire, emploi, solidarité alésienne (Tesa). Un speed dating de l’emploi organisé ce mardi à l’espace Cazot, à Alès (Gard), qui ne rassemble pas que des jeunes à la recherche d’un premier emploi ou d’une formation. Sur place, des parcours variés, avec des candidats venus chercher un poste, mais aussi des pistes pour la suite de leur vie professionnelle.

"On arrive à recruter des candidats", explique Ludo Lombardi de L & B Coaching, alors que le rendez-vous permet aux entreprises et aux organismes de formation d’échanger directement avec les personnes présentes. Un public qui, selon Céline Ringot de CFA-Ecole Cévenole, est "divers, de tout âge". L’occasion de présenter des formations "du CAP au BTS", notamment dans différents secteurs professionnels.

Des profils divers

Parmi les visiteurs, une femme de 60 ans était notamment venue pour "chercher des idées" et pouvoir "se projeter". Un profil qui illustre une autre réalité de la recherche d’emploi : celle de personnes qui, après plusieurs années de vie professionnelle, cherchent elles aussi une nouvelle direction.

À lire aussi : "Faciliter la rencontre entre demandeurs d’emploi et entreprises… " : un grand job dating attendu à Alès pour la rentrée

"Les gens cherchent plus un emploi que la formation", observe par ailleurs Valérie, pour la Chambre de Métiers et de l’Artisanat du Gard. Mais derrière cette recherche, les situations restent différentes : certains veulent travailler rapidement, d’autres se renseignent avant de choisir une formation ou d’envisager une reconversion.

Sin embargo, el mundo de los oficios manuales no parece dejar de atraer a los habitantes de la cuenca, ya sea que salgan de la escuela o se conviertan en profesionales. "Y en esto, la Inteligencia Artificial nunca nos reemplazará", sonríe Céline Ringot.

item.content:encoded:
Cinque minuti per innamorarsi della ricerca! Mettiti comodo, scegli il tuo tavolo e preparati a un faccia a faccia ravvicinato con la scienza. Gli Speed Dating con la Scienza sono incontri lampo dove curiosità e scoperta si fondono: nessuna lezione accademica, solo il racconto vivo di chi esplora il nostro pianeta ogni giorno. Il tempo scorre, le domande corrono… tu a quale tavolo ti siederai?

1) Vulcani nel mondo e in Italia: un viaggio tra i vulcani d’Italia e del mondo per raccontare come la ricerca

scientifica non si limita a studiare i vari processi eruttivi ma raggiunge comunità che vivono in territori unici e spesso complessi, dal punto di vista geografico, ambientale e culturale.

2) Le più grandi bufale sui terremoti (e perché continuiamo a crederci): Si possono prevedere i terremoti? Gli animali sentono in anticipo le scosse? Attraverso brevi confronti in modalità speed date, i partecipanti potranno porre domande direttamente ai ricercatori, discutere dubbi e curiosità e scoprire come funziona la ricerca scientifica.

3) Sotto il mare, oltre i ghiacciai. Racconti di ricerca scientifica in ambienti estremi: Dagli abissi oceanici più oscuri alle distese di ghiaccio dell’Antartide: la ricerca scientifica è la vera esplorazione moderna. In questo speed date faremo un viaggio tra scienza, avventura e meraviglia nei luoghi più remoti e affascinanti della Terra.

4) GNSS ai confini del Mondo: come monitorare i ghiacci estremi: I Poli subiscono, più di ogni altro luogo del nostro pianeta, i cambiamenti climatici che stanno provocando uno scioglimento rapido dei ghiacci. I satelliti del Global Navigation Satellite System (quelli che chiamiamo GPS e usiamo ogni giorno), nati per dirci dove andare, oggi hanno un nuovo ruolo nel monitoraggio dell’ambiente artico. Misurare quanta neve cade ogni anno e vigilare sulla salute del ghiaccio marino. Una tecnologia quotidiana che diventa strumento per monitorare il futuro del nostro clima.

Justine (L’amour est dans le pré) interrompt brusquement son speed dating avec Audran : “Je ne peux pas rester”

Lors du nouvel épisode de L’amour est dans le pré, diffusé ce lundi 14 septembre sur M6, Justine a rencontré ses prétendants. Alors qu’elle faisait la connaissance d’Audran, la jeune femme ne s’est pas sentie bien et a soudainement quitté la péniche.

Un moment pour le moins mouvementé. Après Vincent, son ami de longue date, Justine a pu se lancer dans l’étape des speed datings. Lors du nouvel épisode de L’amour est dans le pré, diffusé ce lundi 14 septembre sur M6, la jeune femme de 34 ans a donné rendez-vous à cinq prétendants sur la péniche Quai Liberté à Liberté. Dépanneur automobile de 27 ans, Audran a été le premier à se lancer dans le bain. Alors qu’il dévoilait les raisons qui l’ont poussé à écrire à la pétillante propriétaire d’une ferme pédagogique, cette dernière a rapidement coupé court à leur échange. «Attends, ne bouge pas. Je ne peux pas rester sur le bateau», a-t-elle lancé, avant de prendre la fuite. Une situation qui a laissé sans voix Karine Le Marchand, qui suivait avec attention ce premier tête-à-tête au côté de Vincent. «Elle est partie !» Face à la surprise de l’animatrice, l’apiculteur a indiqué que Justine a «le mal de mer».

Bien que n’étant pas au meilleur de sa forme, la candidate s’est empressée de retrouver Audran pour poursuivre leur discussion. «Je suis désolée. Est-ce que tu peux te mettre en face comme ça, je ne vois pas l’eau qui est derrière toi», lui a-t-elle demandé, avant de le rassurer : «C’est une horreur mais c’est bon. C’est hyper mal poli, je suis désolée.» Alors qu’elle tentait de reprendre le fil de la conversation, Justine s’est une nouvelle fois éclipsée pour prendre l’air, laissant seul son soupirant. «Le pauvre. C’est la catastrophe. Ce n’est jamais arrivé dans toute l’histoire de L’amour est dans le pré !», a-t-elle indiqué avant de mettre fin à ces dix minutes interminables de speed dating. Si Audran était satisfait de cette rencontre, il en a été tout autre pour Justine.

Passer la publicité

Justine (L’amour est dans le pré) déçue par sa rencontre avec Audran : “Le problème, c’est sa taille”

À l’issue de cet «entretien historique», Karine Le Marchand s’est empressée de retrouver Justine pour un petit débriefing. Dès l’arrivée de la mère d’Alya, la candidate est revenue sur son malaise mais aussi sur un détail qui l’a quelque peu déçu. Si elle souhaite rencontrer un homme aussi grand qu’elle, Audran ne répond malheureusement pas à ce critère. «Le problème, c’est sa taille», a-t-elle avoué, avant d’être coupée net par la présentatrice : «Mais à quel moment on parle on parle de la taille d’un mec ? Là, tu nous l’as castré pour les 30 prochaines années !»

Après cette remarque, le constat a été sans appel pour Justine. «Je lui ai fait le pire date de sa vie». Pour éviter que ce scénario ne se reproduise, Karine Le Marchand lui a proposé d’installer une table dehors. Une suggestion que la principale intéressée a préféré décliner, au grand dam de la présentatrice. Reste à savoir si la suite des speed datings sera aussi chaotique.

item.content:encoded:
L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 : “Ça m’a vraiment déçue !” Pourquoi Justine a très mal vécu son speed-dating ?

Publié le Par Drifa Maza

Ce lundi 14 septembre 2026, Justine sera au cœur de l’intrigue amoureuse dans L’Amour est dans le pré, diffusée sur M6. Toutefois, la candidate n’a pas exactement vécu l’aventure à laquelle elle s’attendait. Pourquoi l’étape du speed dating a-t-elle été compliquée pour elle ? Elle s’est confiée sur ses péripéties, plusieurs mois après le tournage.

Depuis plusieurs semaines maintenant, les bandes-annonces de L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 teasent l’épisode sur Justine à travers des extraits montrant notamment l’épreuve du speed dating. Ce lundi 14 septembre, le quatrième épisode, déjà disponible sur M6+, arrive donc enfin à la télévision, pour le plus grand bonheur des téléspectateurs. Et le moins que l’on puisse dire est que l’émission réserve bien des surprises, autant aux agriculteurs qu’aux fidèles du programme.

Dans l’épisode 4 de la saison 21 de L’Amour est dans le pré, diffusé ce lundi soir dès 21 h 10 sur M6, Justine doit faire face à de nombreuses complications qui ont forcément impacté son aventure.

Sommaire

L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 : le rendez-vous de Justine et Audran a viré au cauchemar…

Les spectateurs remarqueront que lors de son rendez-vous avec Audran, Justine n’est pas restée très immobile. En effet, à plusieurs reprises, la trentenaire a quitté le bateau pour prendre l’air. La raison ? Justine a le mal de mer. Malgré les précautions prises par la production, l’étape de la péniche était obligatoire pour le speed dating. Ainsi, l’agricultrice a dû faire face à ses peurs, mais cela n’a pas duré longtemps.

Interrogée par Télé Star sur cette expérience, Justine a déclaré qu’elle n’a malheureusement pas réussi à surmonter cette épreuve : « J’avais prévenu la production, mais j’ai pensé qu’en étant sur une péniche, à quai, sur la Seine, ça irait. Mais ça a été chaotique. Ça a tangué dans tous les sens, dans mon corps et dans ma tête. Les émotions étaient décuplées et je n’étais pas moi-même. Je lui ai fait vivre le pire date de toute sa vie« .

Voilà donc qui vient instantanément expliquer son comportement particulier envers Audran. Mais ce n’est pas tout ! Justine a également dû faire face à un désistement de dernière minute, qu’elle a encore du mal à digérer aujourd’hui…

Pourquoi Clément s’est désisté dans L’Amour est dans le pré 2026 ?

Alors que Justine s’apprêtait à annoncer à Audran et Clément qu’ils ont été choisis pour l’accompagner à la ferme, le prétendant de 24 ans et éducateur sportif, décide de prendre la main sur la situation en lui annonçant qu’il ne souhaite plus continuer l’émission à ses côtés. « C’était juste pour te dire que je ne vais pas donner suite malheureusement. Je n’ai pas eu ce petit coup de cœur même si tu es une nana magnifique. Je préfère stopper là et ne pas te donner de faux espoirs« , lui a alors annoncé Clément en face-à-face.

Toujours au micro de Télé Star, Justine n’a pas hésité à revenir sur cette trahison : « Ça m’a vraiment déçue. Pour moi, j’étais l’objet d’un pari avec ses copains, et j’ai trouvé ça dénigrant. » Justine était, en effet, tombée sous le charme de Clément, mais l’attirance n’était donc pas réciproque. À voir maintenant ce que l’avenir lui réserve au sein du jeu.

Drifa Maza

Journaliste

Journaliste chez Serieously depuis 2023, Drifa Maza est une grande passionnée de cinéma de toutes les époques, allant de ses débuts silencieux en noir et blanc à aujourd’hui. Toujours à l’affut de l’actualité, elle ne rate aucune sortie ciné et série, et est toujours à la recherche d’une nouveauté et d’un show à binger. Son enfance a été bercée par les films Pixar et l’ère Disney Channel, son adolescence par le genre de la dystopie et les Marvel (qu’elle aime toujours autant) mais c’est surtout en regardant La La Land en 2016 que son amour pour cette industrie est né. Aujourd’hui, Drifa adore partager cette passion et ses connaissances à travers des articles, des quiz et des interviews et rencontres avec les actrices, acteurs et cinéastes comme Celine Song, Danny Boyle ou encore Tom Hardy et Timothée Chalamet, qu’elle admire.
